#1587. Liverpool transfer news: New Alexis Mac Allister contract timeline given as two-year claim made (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 13:45

Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a new contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.

Mac Allister revealed in September that Liverpool were not in a position to offer him a new contract, after the 27-year-old experienced a noticeable decline in individual performance levels in 2025-26.

However, after a positive World Cup with Argentina, Mac Allister has returned to form for Liverpool, scoring five goals and providing one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions so far this season.

The midfielder has started nine of Liverpool's 11 Premier League games under Andoni Iraola and also performed well in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, creating two chances, completing 89% of his passes and winning four of his five ground duels.

Nevertheless, ex-Liverpool midfielder Hamann does not believe that talks over a new deal will begin for another three months, and any extension is only likely to be two years at best.

"They said to him there's no contract now, and he's in his late 20s," Hamann told Sports Mole when asked if Mac Allister had already played his way into a new contract.

"If he carries on performing, if he keeps on scoring goals, then come February, March, April, there might be a time where you say. 'maybe we keep him another two years.' But I don't think there's any rush at the moment."

Mac Allister - who turns 28 on December 24 - has come up with 24 goals and 21 assists in 167 matches for Liverpool since 2023, and he earns £180,000 a week under his current contract terms, according to Capology.

The Argentine's reported salary only makes him the 11th highest-paid player at Liverpool, below new signing Ronald Araujo (£210k) and almost half of what Virgil van Dijk earns (£350k).

Mac Allister's relationship with Ryan Gravenberch blossomed to the maximum in the 2024-25 season, culminating in both midfielders becoming Premier League champions for the first time.

However, Mac Allister's decline from a defensive and box-to-box standpoint was striking; compared to 2024-25, he made 45% fewer tackles and 26% fewer recoveries than in the 2025-26 campaign.

Gravenberch's own form did not help the South American's cause, though, and the latter has had a rejuvenated look about him since the World Cup, immediately earning Iraola's trust in the process.

Mac Allister's availability remains exceptional too, as he has only missed 11 matches for club and country since joining Liverpool and has been involved in every match so far this season.

With Wataru Endo almost certainly on the way out and James McConnell still on the fringes, Liverpool should speed up the process of tying down Mac Allister, lest they risk losing another midfield option in 2027.

United were lucky in the end. Lucky that more than one Red had an off day.

Bradley Barcola had an eventful game. He actually finished it with a wonderful assist for Ngumoha's goal - one where he demonstrated how his pace and intelligence can be impossible to stop.

But in front of goal, he had a nightmare. Barcola couldn't sort his feet out on several occasions, unable to take advantage of the space he'd found in United's defence. With what should have been a fantastic opportunity to show what he can really do, the Frenchman instead looked a level behind when it came to actually scoring goals.

And that's a shame. Because Liverpool spent an awful lot of money and there's no question that Barcola is an elite player. He's just one who hasn't found his finishing in Red.

Barcola himself recognises this, too. He spoke to Canal Plus after the match, as relayed by Fabrizio Romano.

“I’m not happy with how I played," he said. "I know I can do much better and I know what I’m capable of”.

“I came away with an assist, but I could’ve scored three or four goals."

He's right, there's no question there. The important thing from a Liverpool point of view is that the player doesn't need reminding of the standards - he expects to be better than that and expects to put teams to the sword.

Which gives us hope that Barcola will eventually find that finishing at Liverpool. We know he's got the quality and we did see that in the UEFA Champions League with his hat trick against LASK. Now he needs to translate it to the Premier League.

But we believe he'll do that. This was a part demonstration of his ability and the full show is still on its way.

#1585. Premier League identify SIX key refereeing errors in one weekend as boss Howard Webb prepares to appear in front of clubs after Arsenal blunder

Published: 06:08 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 19 November 2026

The Premier League have ruled that referees made a staggering six incorrect decisions in the latest round of matches as officials endured their worst weekend of the season so far.

It was unanimously ruled that referee Farai Hallam should have awarded Kai Havertz a penalty after he was tugged in the area during Arsenal's victory over Hull City, despite being in an offside position.

That is because the laws state that if a foul occurs before an offside offence, a penalty should be awarded.

Although Havertz was in an offside position, he had not committed an offence as he neither played the ball nor interfered with play.

The key match incidents panel (KMI) said: 'Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded.'

Farai Hallam's decision not to award Kai Havertz a penalty was deemed incorrect by the key match incidents panel

Coventry were wrongly denied a spot-kick in their defeat to Everton after James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair

1. Everton vs Coventry City: Frank Lampard's side should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair.

2. Everton vs Coventry City: The Toffees' second goal, scored by Thierno Barry should not have stood as the ball was adjudged to have gone into the back of the net off his hand.

3. Arsenal vs Hull City: Kai Havertz was denied a penalty after being dragged down. The referee did not award a spot-kick because Havertz in an offside position. However, that decision was incorrect, as he was not committing an offside offence and a spot-kick should therefore have been awarded.

4. Crystal Palace vs Liverpool: Palace were awarded a penalty in the last minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool after Milos Kerkez and Dario Osario clashed heads in the penalty area. The panel saw this as a natural coming together.

5. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: A penalty was given after Abdoul Ouattara tumbled over. The referee gave a foul against Lewis Cook despite Ouattara stepping across him.

6. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: Marcus Tavernier should have seen a second yellow card for time-wasting.

They did, however, praise the VAR for asking the referee to review the incident on the monitor, even though Hallam stuck with his on-field call after watching it back.

In the same weekend, Tottenham Hotspur complained to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle's heavy challenge on Mathys Tel's ankle, which forced him off injured.

Spurs felt Bogle should have seen red, particularly after Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for a similar incident the week prior.

Reviewing the decision, the KMI panel were split but eventually concluded that the foul lacked 'the speed, force or intensity' to be considered serious foul play.

Two of the five panellists, however, felt that the challenge merited a red card.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace's consolation penalty in the 92nd minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool should never have been awarded.

The KMI panel unanimously agreed the referee was wrong to award a penalty when Milos Kerkez and Dario Osorio clashed heads while contesting the ball, with contact inevitable given both players were jumping.

However, VAR's decision not to intervene was supported because it was not a 'clear and obvious error'.

It is the second penalty incident in as many weeks that went against Liverpool after Alexander Isak was wrongfully denied a spot-kick against Arsenal.

On the opposite side of Merseyside, James Tarkowski was fortunate not to concede a penalty for pulling Caleb Yirenkyi's hair during Everton's win over Coventry City, with the score still 0-0 at the time. The panel found that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty while Tarkowski should have been booked.

Last season, that incident would likely have resulted in a straight red card. However, the guidance changed this term with red cards only brandished for excessive force.

Thierno Barry's goal that gave Everton the lead faced scrutiny as three panellists believed it should have been disallowed on the pitch, with the 'balance of probability suggesting the ball accidentally struck Barry's hand before directly entering the goal'.

There were also two incorrect decisions in Bournemouth's victory over Ipswich Town.

Bournemouth defender Marcus Tavernier should have been sent off for a second yellow card in the 96th minute for delaying the restart during their 2-1 win, the panel found. However, it was a close call as the panel voted 3-2 against the decision.

Ipswich's scored penalty was also deemed wrongly awarded, with Abdoul Ouattara stepping across Lewis Cook to win the spot-kick rather than being fouled by the defender.

The KMI panel consists of a representative from the Premier League and Pro Ref alongside three former managers or players and meets after every round of Premier League matches to evaluate significant refereeing decisions.

Ref boss Howard Webb will speak to Premier League clubs at a routine meeting on Thursday

While the panel is not new, this is the first season their findings have been publicly released in Pro Ref's drive for greater transparency and accountability.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb is due to appear in front of clubs on Thursday at a routine Premier League meeting.

And in more positive news for Webb, he will be able to share that VAR delays are down this season after increasing the bar for interventions.

Meanwhile, the KMI panel have assessed 296 decisions this season - only six of which have been judged to be wrong post-VAR.

#1584. Man Utd make decision on what to do next after Leny Yoro's controversial red card against Liverpool

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:57, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 14:51

Manchester United have reportedly notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card.

The centre-back was sent off during Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday after bringing down Alexander Isak as the striker raced through on goal.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into the contest, a moment that significantly altered the complexion of the game as Liverpool enjoyed greater possession and created better opportunities.

While Man Utd could arguably have done more to frustrate the Reds, there is little doubt that Yoro's dismissal had a major bearing on the outcome.

According to Sky Sports, the Red Devils intend to appeal Yoro's dismissal, with Mauricio Pochettino offering his interpretation of the incident after the game.

The main point of contention is whether the foul constituted a clear denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with questions surrounding whether Isak was actually in control of the ball.

Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations when determining whether a player should be sent off for Denying an Obvious Goal-Scoring Opportunity (DOGSO) is whether the attacking player had control of the ball.

Pochettino not only questioned that aspect of the decision but also highlighted the referee's failure to penalise Jeremy Jacquet for his challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments earlier.

It remains to be seen how the FA will assess the incidents, although former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher has backed the on-field decisions in both cases.

Unless the decision is overturned following an appeal, Yoro is set to serve a one-match domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban, as his denial of a obvious goalscoring opportunity was a non-violent offence.

While the defender is available to face Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, he will miss Man United's next Premier League fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro will then be available to return to Premier League action on December 2 when Pochettino's side travel to St James' Park to take on Newcastle United.

The Red Devils are now without a win in their last nine Premier League matches and have slipped to 19th in the table, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

#1581. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1580. Man City charges: Jeremy Doku's response to “juicy” discussion on guilty Premier League verdict

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 13:59

Jeremy Doku was the latest Manchester City player to be questioned on his thoughts regarding the club’s Premier League financial charges case during a press conference on Monday.

An independent commission has found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

In a verdict delivered at the end of September, the Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 campaigns.

Man City have repeatedly expressed their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

Should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, the club would be in danger of a plethora of possible sanctions, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

On the pitch, Man City have recently suffered a dip in form, failing to win any of their last four Premier League games (D1 L3), but manager Enzo Maresca played down suggestions that the 115 charges case is distracting his players - something Didi Hamann disagrees with.

Since September’s verdict, the likes of captain Ruben Dias and star striker Erling Haaland have faced questions on the ongoing legal case, and Doku is now the latest City star to be asked for his views on the matter.

However, Doku politely declined to comment on the club’s situation and was keen to discuss on-field matters only when speaking to the media ahead of City’s Champions League clash with Napoli on Tuesday.

“I know this is all juicy for you guys, but we have a big week; Napoli tomorrow, and then Arsenal," the Belgium international told reporters on Monday.

"So I think there's enough to speak about there instead of speaking about the charges. I'm not the person to speak about the charges, so with all respect I don't really want to be on that topic. We can speak about football, that's no problem."

In August, just a month before the guilty verdict was published, Doku extended his contract with Man City until the summer of 2031, and the winger has no regrets over his decision.

"I signed because I was happy to sign. I didn't think about anything else,” Doku clearly stated after being asked whether the charges came into his conversations over a new contract.

"I don't think it was a difficult thing for me. When you look at this club, how big of a club it is, the trophies they won and everything, it was an easy choice for me.

"I was happy here, I am happy here, I have a wife here, a son, it was an easy choice for me. So I didn't think a lot, obviously everything needed to be right for me to sign, but as soon as everything was right on both sides, it was an easy choice for me."

Assessing Man City’s season so far from an individual and collective perspective, Doku added: "I think I can do better. I started off with an injury this season, then came back well.

“And then the team, we did well with the first seven [Premier League] games where we won, and afterwards it was a bit more tough. As everyone knows, at the moment it's a bit more difficult, but I'm sure we'll bounce back, me as well."

Doku is a strong contender to start for Man City in their Champions League clash against Napoli, with the Citizens seeking to move one step closer to automatic last-16 qualification having already won three of their first four League Phase matches.

Maresca, meanwhile, has provided a positive update on the fitness of right-back Matheus Nunes, who missed the 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham last weekend.

#1578. Inside Xabi Alonso's goalkeeping headache: Why Blues boss could go against the fans' view and pick volatile Emiliano Martinez over 21-year-old prodigy Mike Penders

Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026

A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

One is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career. The other is a 34-year-old Argentinian who won the 2022 World Cup and has appeared 234 times in the Premier League.

We mention those brief backgrounds because when assessing who will give him the greater chance of stopping Leeds United from scoring on Saturday, Xabi Alonso takes them into account. Indeed, Alonso told us so while covering Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

One conversation with the manager was centred on his goalkeeper options. At that time, they were Penders and Robert Sanchez.

Alonso praised Penders’ potential but explained to us how highly he values ‘experience’ in his goalkeeper. ‘To have this security in goal is important,’ he insisted when asked.

Sanchez was indeed nominated as his No 1 for their first fixture of the Premier League season at Fulham. The 29-year-old Spaniard had a stinker, which led to him being loaned to Como. It is a straightforward loan, and he has been second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas, so there is a chance he will be back at Chelsea next summer, but that is a problem for another day.

A Daily Mail Sport poll of almost 2,000 Chelsea fans resulted in 57.9 per cent voting in favour of Mike Penders (above) keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Martinez is available for the first time since breaking his jaw at Hill Dickinson Stadium

Martinez arrived from Aston Villa for £7.5million, was told he would be Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, and is now available again. He is able to play without a protective mask, as he did while representing Argentina in their 7-0 friendly win over Costa Rica on Tuesday night.

It was his first appearance since breaking his jaw at Everton and having surgery exactly a month prior. He headed back to London after that victory to return to Chelsea, presumably under the impression that he will be playing against Leeds come Saturday.

It is Alonso who will have the ultimate say on who goes in goal, in conjunction with his head of goalkeeping, Ben Roberts, and assistant goalkeeping coach, James Russell. That decision will be communicated with his chosen goalkeeper in the build-up, though Alonso is unlikely to tell us when we ask him at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

One insider consulted this week said his suspicion is the Argentinian will make an immediate return because it would create a headache for Alonso. Martinez is a big character, volatile, and, if reduced to second choice, would not be pleased.

Statistically, Leeds cross the ball more than most in the Premier League, which could be more challenging for Penders than Martinez.

Filling in for Martinez, Penders punched the ball into his own goal on his first league start for Chelsea in a 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur.

However, he impressed against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, then Manchester United and Sunderland in the Premier League. He won the Save of the Month award for October for denying Bryan Mbeumo at Stamford Bridge.

Penders won October's Save of the Month award for denying Man United's Bryan Mbeumo

Penders is clearly a terrific talent, and it would be tempting to continue to show trust in him by having him face Leeds. Chelsea then face Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace, Liverpool and Manchester City in a rush of fixtures as we head into December.

It is a big decision to be made by Alonso, and would take bravery for him to stick with his prodigy in Penders, when we know the experience of the proven Martinez weighs heavy in his mind.

Chelsea vice captain Moises Caicedo is to be checked over at Cobham after a small injury scare while the influential midfielder was away with Ecuador.

Caicedo would be expected to wear the armband at Leeds in Reece James’ ongoing absence. He is set to return to the training ground on Thursday to be assessed.

The 25-year-old played 84 minutes in Ecuador’s first fixture of the break, a 2-0 victory against Costa Rica in which he scored. However, he then asked to be substituted at half-time of their 2-0 win over Bolivia, which ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning. Captaining his country, it was believed to be due to a small physical complaint.

Meanwhile, Chelsea have been looking at the midfield market in the build-up to this January after they missed out on bolstering their options in the summer when Enzo Fernandez was sold to Manchester City. They retain an interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

#1576. Galatasaray vs. Aston Villa: Unai Emery claims unusual Champions League preparation 'will not be an excuse'

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 14:03

Unai Emery has played down the significance of Aston Villa's unusual preparations for Tuesday's Champions League fixture at Galatasaray.

Having put together a five-game winless streak, Emery is coming under more scrutiny than he usually receives at Villa Park.

Victory at Rams Park would effectively guarantee Villa a place in the top 24 of the League Phase table and a spot in the knockout stages.

However, Villa have been required to change from the standard routine for a Champions League away game due to the condition of Galatasaray's pitch.

Although the match is not at risk of being postponed, UEFA has informed Villa that they cannot train at RAMS Park before the game, and the Premier League club opted against taking up the option of training at a different Turkish location.

Instead, Villa conducted their final training session at their own training facilities, while Emery held his pre-match press conference in Birmingham rather than Istanbul.

The Spaniard insisted that the amended schedule cannot be used as "an excuse" if Villa do not earn a result versus the Super Lig champions.

He told reporters: "It's not changing our usual way. We prefer to train here at Bodymoor and then travel to the country.

"We are doing some exceptions when we are playing a long way with a time change, we are training in the country - we did it last year at Fenerbahce.

"Of course if we could train at the stadium maybe we would decide to, but it's not changing our routine.

"It's not an excuse because it's for both teams. We are ready and we are focused and analysing the opponent."

Not only do Villa face Galatasaray this week, they make the trip to play Ipswich Town on Saturday evening in a key Premier League match.

Villa remain with just three wins from 11 matches in England's top flight, and failure to prevail against either Galatasaray or Ipswich would leave Emery going seven matches without a win when he is due to sign a new contract.

While Emery has total backing from the club's hierarchy and supporters, it is clear he needs to end their current run of form as soon as possible.

#1575. Journalist confirms it: Liverpool are in talks to agree unthinkable deal

Liverpool are now in talks to complete a deal that was previously though to be unthinkable. There's been a big change of plans.

Liverpool essentially had to tear up most of their plans after last season. Arne Slot left as head coach, after all, and then Richard Hughes was out as sporting director after the summer.

And that's not to mention the fact that last season was a failure. Liverpool invested enormously in a new team but quite unequivocally got worse - the grand plan was not working.

That led to even more heavy investment in 2026 but with Julian Ward now at the helm as sporting director, he has the power to move things in a different direction. And it sounds as though he's trying to do exactly that.

Starting with one deal that felt unthinkable a couple of years ago.

Essentially no one at Liverpool though Alisson Becker would get a new contract back in 2024. You can see that quite clearly: they signed Giorgi Mamardashvili and then stored him at Valencia for a year.

The plan was always for Mamardashvili to take over as no.1, potentially last season. That didn't happen and Liverpool still haven't made him the first-choice between the sticks.

The Reds plainly laid out the plan in the summer, though. Lucca Brughmans signed for the future, with the Club Brugge goalkeeper joining after this season - he was supposed to be Mamardashvili's understudy post-Alisson.

Instead? Alisson looks set to remain the first choice goalkeeper for at least another couple of years. A move that looked unthinkable as Liverpool signed two new goalkeepers is now on the brink of reality.

#1573. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta issues David Raya injury update after worrying photo emerges

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 14:15

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund but appears to have avoided a serious injury, Mikel Arteta has announced.

The Spain international collided with Newcastle United striker Will Osula in the second half of Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw and had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya was in visible pain as an Arsenal physio supported his arm and shoulder, and Arteta admitted at full time that his number one having to come off was "not good news".

The Arsenal boss also revealed that Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to assess the seriousness of the issue, and on the same day, he was photographed with his arm in a sling in London.

@TouchlineX Raya yesterday in Oxford Circus... https://t.co/6NVmuNDLzZ

However, speaking to reporters in his pre-game press conference, Arteta delivered a reassuring update on Raya, who has seemingly avoided a fracture or dislocation and will not need to go under the knife.

"He’s not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected," Arteta told the media.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test we have done shows something that is much more encouraging. There is no need for surgery. Tomorrow we will have more tests and we will know [more]."

Arteta did not directly rule Raya out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester City either, potentially handing Arsenal a monumental boost ahead of the visit of Enzo Maresca's side.

The 31-year-old has already kept 10 clean sheets in 16 appearances for the Gunners this season, and he is also believed to have agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal; his current deal expires in 2028.

Raya has only missed one Arsenal game through injury since originally joining on loan from Brentford in January 2023 - the 5-1 EFL Cup third-round win over Bolton Wanderers in September 2024.

With Raya sidelined, Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to make just his second Champions League start for Arsenal on Tuesday, after appearing in January's 3-2 victory over Kairat Almaty.

However, Arteta could throw a curveball and select Illan Meslier, whose first and only appearance for the Gunners so far came in their horrendous EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

The Frenchman has also never played in the Champions League in his career, while Kepa has appeared in the competition 22 times and was Chelsea's starting goalkeeper during their run to the 2022-23 quarter-finals.

As the latter has also held his position as Arteta's number two despite Meslier's arrival, there should be no doubt over Arsenal's starting goalkeeper against Borussia Dortmund.

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release

In a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The new boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor announced that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game

'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, said with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' said Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'

New York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall said. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event

Department store chain John Lewis said it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

#1570. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Counter-attacking clinic sees Rossoneri run riot

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

However, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

The frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

Frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

Just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

The two-goal lead was very quickly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

Amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

The change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

There was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for company, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

With 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

#1569. Man United predicted lineup vs. Sporting Lisbon: De Ligt, Zirkzee decisions, Cunha blow

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 14:45, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:11

Mauricio Pochettino could be without as many as seven Manchester United players for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Former Sporting midfielder Manuel Ugarte (knee), Carlos Baleba (hamstring) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Luke Shaw (muscle), Marcus Rashford (hip) and Karl Darlow (knee) are all doubtful and will need assessing ahead of kickoff.

Matheus Cunha scored two late goals in Man United’s 3-2 comeback victory over Roma on matchday four, but he was then sent off for two bookable offences and will now serve a one-match suspension on Wednesday.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, is available to return to the UCL squad after serving his own one-game ban following a red card against Atletico Madrid last month – he also received a straight red card in Man United’s heavy 4-0 Premier League defeat to Liverpool on Sunday, but will instead serve a domestic ban for that dismissal.

Yoro could therefore continue as a centre-back against Sporting, with Pochettino to weigh up whether to stick with a back three/five system with wing-backs or revert to a four-man defence.

Matthijs de Ligt was handed his first PL start in 357 games by Pochettino after recovering from a long-term injury, but the Dutchman endured a difficult return to the Red Devils side and may be pulled out of the starting lineup in midweek.

Harry Maguire would be the most likely name to replace De Ligt and could start as one of three central defenders next to Yoro and Lisandro Martinez, with Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu operating as wing-backs.

Noussair Mazraoui is an alternative who could start as a right or left-sided full-back in a back four, or as a wing-back, with Dalot potentially operating on the opposite side, allowing Dorgu to push further forward and play in an attacking role.

Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and captain Bruno Fernandes are expected to continue in their central midfield roles, the latter is set to face his former club for the first time since leaving to join Man United in January 2020.

Bryan Mbeumo could retain his starting spot as a centre-forward, but Pochettino may be tempted to hand Joshua Zirkzee a rare start up front, with Mbeumo moving over to the right side of attack. However, Amad Diallo could instead play on the right which would likely keep Mbeumo through the middle.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Dalot, Mainoo, Tielemans, Dorgu; Mbeumo, Fernandes; Zirkzee

#1568. Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz

Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

News of new contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s new contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on new contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree new terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

He told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

Now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The plan to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

The biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

The injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next big decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain important to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

Mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed new long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Big Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

The environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be said for stars at every club in the league.

There’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his new midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager said: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement

The collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal

This season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

#1567. Rangers vs Aberdeen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34

Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.

Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.

Although missing out on European football came as a major blow to Rangers at the time, it has enabled Derek McInnes's side to build up a head of steam on the domestic front.

Rangers have put together a 13-match unbeaten streak since that exit to Jablonec in the Conference League playoff round, recording 11 wins and two draws.

While being held to a 2-2 draw at Hearts before the November international break frustrated McInnes, Rangers have responded with a victory over Aberdeen in the League Cup and successive top-flight triumphs.

A 2-0 success at St Mirren was followed by an hard-earned 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday, Rangers sealing the three points through an 88th-minute own goal.

Eight of Rangers' 13 league matches have been played away from Ibrox, giving them a chance to make the most of competing on home territory, with seven goals being scored in their last two such games in the Scottish Premiership.

Over the international break, Liechtenstein legend Mario Frick was named as the new Aberdeen head coach.

The surprise development was followed by Frick delivering a 4-2 victory at Kilmarnock in his first game in charge.

A much-needed win has led to the Dons moving into eighth spot, albeit still just three points above the relegation zone.

With Aberdeen having lost five of the six matches preceding his arrival, Frick will not be getting carried away with three points versus bottom-of-the-table opposition.

Nevertheless, Aberdeen have now accumulated seven points from their most recent four away games in the Scottish Premiership, something which cannot be ignored by their hosts.

If McInnes makes any changes to his Rangers XI, Findlay Curtis and Kevin Kelsy are favourites to be introduced in the final third.

While Cameron Devlin is making progress in his recovery from injury, this game is expected to come too soon for the midfielder. The same applies to Lawrence Shankland, who has recently returned to light training after a significant hamstring injury.

Ryan Naderi has contributed either a goal or assist in eight of his last nine Scottish Premiership appearances.

Afeez Aremu, Findlay Marshall and Ayoub Mouloua are all options to return for Aberdeen after they made an impact from the substitutes' bench at Kilmarnock.

Connor Ronan remains an injury doubt after missing that fixture, while this match comes too soon for defender Mats Knoester. Chris Cadden is pushing for a return to the squad after a hamstring issue.

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Rommens; Neil, Raskin; Bouanani, Naderi, Findlay; Kelsy

Muller; Devlin, Milne, Molloy, Guinness-Walker; Lyons, Aremu, Briedl; Marshall; Mouloua, Nisbet

With Aberdeen having made a positive start to life under Frick, they will back themselves to earn a result at Ibrox. However, given the chance to move within a point of Celtic, we feel that Rangers will do just enough to secure three points in a competitive fixture.

#1566. Player Ratings: AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone – Rabiot unstoppable; super attack

AC Milan clinched a comfortable win against Frosinone and individual brilliance certainly had a hand in that. Below are the player ratings for the Rossoneri.

Ahead of what will be a busy month, Milan knew that a win tonight would do them a lot of good, so that’s exactly what they managed to achieve. Goals from Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic set them up nicely, as well as an early own-goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

👔 Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.

Maignan (6): I’m not sure he could have done better on the goal, as it was really hard to predict where the cross would end up. Anyway, he made a couple of decent stops and was good with his feet, even if there was a scare in the first half.

Gila (6.5): Let me just say straight off the bat that he wasn’t far away from a 7. However, I think he could have done better to stop the cross on the goal conceded, and he had a few really poor passes as well. On the plus side, he was decent in possession overall and had a key clearance in the second half.

De Winter (6.5): He continues to marshal the defence well, though he lacked concentration on a few occasions today. It didn’t prove to be costly and similarly to Gila, there was definitely more good than harm, but the rating is affected a tad.

Diawara (6.5): I don’t think he could have got to the ball quicker on the goal, not to mention that it’s hard to anticipate such a deflection. As far as I’m concerned, it was solid defending from him, including some nice clearances to stop a few dangerous crosses.

Bartesaghi (6): Defensively he did okay, which was all that was required of him, but the main contributions were in attack. I think we saw some really good runs forward from him, although the crosses had mixed results. It seems fair with a 6 for him.

Moreira (7.5): His run before the second goal was crucial, of course, and he also managed to get an assist (good pass in the end, as VAR confirmed). For a higher rating, I would have liked to see more sharpness in the final third, as he had a couple of very good shooting opportunities that he missed.

Modric (8): My word, the pass before the first goal was just magnificent! That alone shows just how much he means to this team, but he also continued to do well with his passing and movement after that. For me, the rating does deserve to be that high, but maybe I’m blinded by the aforementioned pass.

Musah (7): He did really well to unleash Moreira just before the second goal, playing it perfectly. On the goal conceded, it was just unlucky in my opinion, he did everything right by getting a toe on it. The block at the start of the second half was just brilliant too, showcasing good defensive skills.

Pulisic (7.5): Amorim always says he lets the pitch do the talking and that was the case today. He wasn’t flashy by any means, but did very good work in silence (such as the movement before the own-goal) and was eventually rewarded with the goal. Stunning finish by the way. An 8 perhaps?

Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

Ramos (7.5): Finally, back on target! Overall, it was a very encouraging one for him as the goal was the result of great positioning and hard work, which helped on the other goals too (opening up space). He could have had a second too if he hadn’t been stopped by the referee.

Jashari (7): That’s one way to make an impact! The finish was fantastic and really surprised the goalkeeper. He had a few more good runs after that, so this was definitely a performance that he can build on.

Cisse (7): It was an easy finish on the goal, it has to be said, but he still timed the run very well. He also showed off some good understanding in the centre-forward, which was nice to see. It wasn’t nice to see the unnecessary yellow card at the end, though.

Pavlovic (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Estupinan (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Hutchinson (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.
